summary: Ran comprehensive backend pytest suite (19 tests, all PASS) covering auth for all 5 roles, dashboard, seeded jobs, Excel-vs-App validation (has_reference=true, 0 FAIL for BOTH CY/219.03 and CY/212.01 - proves calc engine matches Excel exactly), calculation endpoint, full workflow (submit-review -> review -> approve -> PDF -> public verify), RBAC enforcement (viewer 403 on writes, reviewer 403 on approve, technician can create), audit trail of reading changes, masters validity. Verified frontend loads: login, dashboard stats + recent jobs + master validity widget render; Jobs list shows 2 seeded rows; JobDetail tabs (Overview/Readings/Calculation/Excel vs App/Certificate/Audit) render; Validation tab renders 35 rows for CY/212.01 (5 points x 7 params); Calculation tab shows 5 calc-point cards; navigation to Masters works. Public /verify endpoint correctly omits customer name/address. Certificate PDF is a valid PDF (%PDF header, application/pdf). Fixed one critical login bug during testing (see updated_files).

critical.issue: FIXED. LoginIn used pydantic EmailStr which REJECTS the demo domain '@yog.local' (reserved TLD) - returned 422 for technician/reviewer/signatory/viewer, meaning 4 of 5 demo users could NOT log in at all. Changed EmailStr -> str in server.py. Root cause: pydantic email_validator treats .local as special-use reserved TLD. Long-term either use different demo domain (e.g., @yog.test - actually also reserved; use @example.com) or keep permissive str. Currently permissive.

Bug: server.py line 381 calls `body.job_no` in audit() but JobCreate model has NO job_no field. Creating a job via POST /api/jobs will raise AttributeError (500). Frontend NewJob.jsx must currently work around this or the endpoint never worked. Add `job_no: str = ""` to JobCreate.

minor.issue: ReadingsUpdate/PointIn does not include `excel_reference`, so any technician readings edit STRIPS the seeded excel_reference ground-truth from a point (pydantic drops unknown fields). Observed: audit test edited CY/212.01 readings; validation subsequently returns has_reference=false. Not a prod issue for real jobs (which never have excel_reference), but preserves stored reference by using $set on specific fields or by carrying excel_reference through PointIn.
Approval is irreversible per spec; no cancel/rejection path after certification other than certificate cancellation. Confirmed behavior; documented.

issues: When excel_reference is absent, the 'Excel' and 'Difference' columns render em-dashes and status N/A - acceptable, but consider hiding the table or showing a clearer banner (currently shows 'No Excel reference values stored for this job.' - good).

action_items: Add `job_no: str = ''` (and any other required fields) to JobCreate model in /app/backend/server.py to fix POST /api/jobs (currently would raise AttributeError on audit call).

Decide long-term auth: revert email: str -> EmailStr and change demo user emails away from .local (e.g., @example.com), OR keep permissive str validation. Test agent chose permissive str to unblock demo credentials from problem statement.
Optional: preserve excel_reference on PUT /readings so the Excel-vs-App comparison survives readings edits.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py line 381 references undefined body.job_no - latent 500 on job creation.
PointIn used both for create AND readings-update means updates silently strip fields like excel_reference; consider separate ReadingPointIn.
compute_job is called on every /validation and /certificate/pdf request - fine for MVP but heavy for long point lists; consider caching last computed result.
clean() strips password_hash but does not strip other sensitive fields (e.g., audit reason on certificate cancel is exposed via public verify? No - verify() constructs response manually, OK).
seed() runs on startup; safe reseed logic gated by db.jobs.count_documents({}) > 0 - correct.
JWT set via cookies (httpOnly, secure, samesite=none) AND access_token in response - good for dual bearer/cookie use.

rca of the issue: Login 422 for demo users: pydantic EmailStr uses email_validator which rejects reserved TLDs like .local per RFC 2606. Fix applied by changing to plain str; alternate is to use a non-reserved TLD for demo accounts. Reproduction: POST /api/auth/login with {email:'technician@yog.local'} -> 422. Mitigation done in server.py.
